item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 摩托车新手上路日志 KTM 390 SMC 两个月前搬到加州的时候出于好奇，在驾照申请表上勾了个摩托。笔试时傻眼了。网上的测试题库太小
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
摩托车新手上路日志 KTM 390 SMC

两个月前搬到加州的时候出于好奇，在驾照申请表上勾了个摩托。笔试时傻眼了。网上的测试题库太小，毫无帮助。我问大姐能不能把摩托车划掉，就给我汽车的驾照。她说对不起，交40块重新填表排队。
我服了，回家把DMV的摩托手册读了两遍，第二天一次通过。然后呢？然后还是不能给我驾照的塑料卡。原因是还需要通过路试，或MSP。

我当天点了个San Jose两天的MSP，$450。一周后上课。一开始选摩托的时候我反应太慢，只剩下了一台本田CRF150。我觉得座位太高，但是教练说你能行，所以我信了。结果一上车就翻车，然后换了Rebel 250。一周后收到认证。两周后拿到驾照加M1。

本来想买一台越野的去泥地里浪。后来嫌麻烦，就买了一台Super Moto类别的KTM 390 SMC。装备上花了2000多。买了200多的手套，200多带护垫的牛仔裤，300多的鞋子，200多带护垫的上衣，TechAir 5气囊，LS2 Carbon Thunder头盔。这头盔竟然要700。当时纯粹是看上了他的名字和外形。我的车是手动的LS3，所以觉得头盔上如果写LS2有点好玩（我太无聊了）。

已经摔了3次。第一次是提车时，车停在坡上，车头朝下，我需要立即左转。由于座位高度不适应，一启动就往左摔，气囊没爆，但是离合器杆断了一截。然后把车扶起直接在没导航的情况下骑了10英里到家。

第二次是上立交桥的时候堵车，在弯道上停下，然后因为误判了坡度，车不动的情况下往右摔。这次气囊爆了但是车没事。一位好心的黑叔叔帮我把车扶起，然后就骑回家了。

花了140买了个新的气囊发射器。离合器杆花了10。越野用的护手花了100多。行车记录仪200多。车轮和车身划片总共200多。

昨天是第三次摔，有点疼。我在Cavaleras Road上以20英里的时速进了一个15英里往左的弯。进弯时太靠右，后轮碰到了一层土以后开始侧滑。车碰地时手柄插进土里然后把车身瞬间弹回直立状态，同时把我的右腿弹飞。我空中转了半圈以后懵了。结果是左肘和左膝擦伤。裤子和夹克都没破。皮是被衣服内部擦破的。当时没穿气囊，所以不用换发射器。车毫发未损，直接骑回家了。

现在车骑了300英里。600英里第一次保养时再更新。

➖ 传达室 ➖

item.title: Avi Chawla Coding agent just got a lot more independent: They can now do the one
item.description:
Avi Chawla
Coding agent just got a lot more independent:

They can now do the one thing they used to need you for.

When you ask an agent to build an app, it can write the schema, the routes, and the data layer in a few minutes.

But then it needs a database, and everything stops since someone has to open a browser, create an account, provision a database, set up a user, and paste the connection string back into the session.

Those steps were built for a human, so the agent just waits for you to complete them.

MongoDB just solved that with Atlas Ephemeral Clusters.

Now, your agent can make one API call, and Atlas returns a live database in under a minute.

Your agent saves the connection string, allowing you to keep building on a real MongoDB Atlas cluster.

You can learn more here: https://t.co/1AvhBezHTV

The part I like most is that the agent can create the database cluster and work with the data, but only a human can make the decision to claim it and take ownership.

If you don’t claim it, the cluster pauses after 48 hours and deletes itself after 7 days, so abandoned experiments clean themselves up automatically.

If you claim it, it becomes a permanent free Atlas cluster with the same data and the same connection string.

So the agent handles the setup end-to-end, and you only step in once the project is worth keeping.

Atlas Ephemeral Clusters are in public preview, and the docs shared above walk you through the full flow.

The video below shows this in action, and I worked with the MongoDB team to put this together.

If you are building with coding agents, the next step is getting several of them to work together on one project.

I wrote a full breakdown of how Claude Code handles that with subagents and agent teams.

It covers when a subagent is enough, when you need a team of agents that coordinate with each other, and how each setup manages context and hands off work.

Read it below.

https://t.co/lVnuSmNYo7 - Avi Chawla

item.title: Daily Dose of Data Science Google open-sourced Harness². (turn any harness into
item.description:
Daily Dose of Data Science
Google open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://t.co/7CkAGptSOC

item.content:encoded:
Daily Dose of Data Science
Google open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://t.co/7CkAGptSOC
